claims.text: Decorator pattern: a class implements the same interface as another object, holds that object, and adds its own work before or after passing each call on to it.
claims.source_hint: glossary decorator-pattern; GoF book, Decorator pattern

claims.text: At stage-2 ProductCache is declared `public sealed class ProductCache(IProductRepository inner, IConnectionMultiplexer redis, ILogger<ProductCache> logger) : IProductRepository`; it declares no base class.

ProductCache.FindAsync first reads product:{id} from Redis; on a hit it returns the copy without calling inner; on a miss it calls inner.FindAsync(id), stores the product only when it is not null, and returns it.
ProductCache.UpdatePriceAsync calls inner.UpdatePriceAsync(id, priceVnd) first and calls RemoveAsync($"product:{id}") only when the returned product is not null.
EfProductRepository is sealed, takes only DonHangDbContext, and its FindAsync is one line (db.Products.FindAsync(id)); the file does not mention Redis.
In C#, a non-abstract class that implements an interface must provide every member of that interface, so ProductCache must have FindAsync and UpdatePriceAsync.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: interface keyword / interface implementation

claims.text: In C#, a class declared sealed cannot be used as a base class, so no subclass of EfProductRepository can be declared.

AddScoped<EfProductRepository>() registers the class as its own service type; AddScoped<IProductRepository>(factory) makes the container call the factory to build an IProductRepository; provider is the container and GetRequiredService<T>() asks it for a T.

ProductsController's constructor takes DonHangDbContext db and IProductRepository products; Get(id) uses FindAsync, the StaffOnly PATCH uses UpdatePriceAsync, and the paged List reads db.Products directly (not cached).

At stage-2, `git grep -n "IProductRepository" -- DonHang.Api` prints ProductsController.cs lines 12 (comment) and 15 (constructor); `git grep -n "new ProductCache" -- "*.cs"` prints one line, ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:44: plus that line's text.
claims.source_hint: run in examples/don-hang at stage-2 (verified locally with git grep on the tag); git-grep docs, pathspec

claims.text: Because the wrapped object only has to be an IProductRepository and a decorator is one, decorators can be stacked (e.g. a timing wrapper around ProductCache) without changing the class at the centre or the caller.
Putting the cache in its own class that implements the same interface, instead of editing the query method, keeps caching changes out of the class that holds the queries.
Holding the wrapped object through the interface, rather than subclassing, lets one decorator wrap any implementation, including another decorator; a subclass is tied to one class.
